question: The Deflection Factor (G) of a CRT (where s is the defection sensitivity) is defined as:
solution:
The correct answer is __G = 1/s**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deflection Factor (G)__ is inversely proportional to deflection sensitivity (s).
 
• Mathematically, it is represented as G = 1/s.
 
• Deflection sensitivity (s) refers to the degree of movement of the electron beam for a given voltage.
 
• Higher sensitivity results in lower deflection factor and vice versa.
 
• It is an important parameter in Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Deflection Sensitivity:**
 
 
• It measures the displacement of the electron beam per unit deflection voltage.
 
• It is commonly used in oscilloscopes and display devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of CRT:**
 
 
• CRT technology is used in television screens, oscilloscopes, and radar displays.
 
• Modern devices largely use LCD and LED technologies, but CRT is still relevant in some specialized applications.
